mandate: Post WWIll, nations lie fragmented. Global institutions and pillars of peace have collapsed. The Earth grows increasingly uninhabitable by the day. Set in November 2060, the Futuristic Joint Crisis Cabinets will test your ability to handle what seems to be humanity’s end—a global fertility crisis, AI data centres consuming water by the gallons, the militarisation of biotechnology and augmented soldiers, and what seems to be the intricate genetic technology that will fix it all. Traverse the dystopia by joining forces with The Sovereign Council as you negotiate resources with nascent States. Unless, of course, you seek an alternative that requires no negotiation at all... or join The Consortium of Human Continuity, and navigate the workings of autonomous AI archives, newly founded religions, and clandestine entities with seemingly innocuous intentions. Will you abandon the means we deem atrocious today for an end that outweighs it all tomorrow, or will you crack under the weight of the world?

The First Committee of the United Nations General Assembly, commonly known as DISEC, is responsible for addressing international peace, security, disarmament, and emerging threats to global stability. As one of the six main committees of the General Assembly, DISEC serves as a platform where member states debate pressing security challenges, formulate international norms, and propose mechanisms aimed at preventing conflict and maintaining peace.

The committee examines both traditional and emerging security concerns, ranging from conventional weapons and nuclear proliferation to cyber warfare and autonomous military technologies. While its resolutions are not legally binding, DISEC's recommendations significantly influence international security policies and future diplomatic negotiations.

Cyber warfare has become a major challenge to international peace and security, as states increasingly use cyber operations to disrupt critical infrastructure, steal information, and influence other countries. One of the biggest challenges is attribution, or identifying who is responsible for a cyberattack. Anonymity, proxies, false-flag techniques, and limited access to intelligence make this difficult. This creates challenges for accountability, international cooperation, and deciding what a lawful and appropriate response should be. The United Nations has developed voluntary norms through the GGE and OEWG processes, but disagreements remain over attribution, international law, and how states should respond to state-sponsored cyberattacks.
agenda: Establishing International Norms for Attribution and Response to State-Sponsored Cyberattacks

mandate:
In 1945, ECOFIN was founded as the Second Committee of the United Nations General Assembly. Its membership is open to all 193 member states. The committee addresses issues related to development economics and international finance.

Its actions involve encouraging funding for development projects and highlighting areas for sustainable development. Instruments typically used by the committee include debate and resolutions. Creating effective policies that use these instruments requires tying in academic work, so ECOFIN also hosts speakers with expertise in creating relevant policies. Since the resolutions written by the committee do not have the power of legislation, the committee aims for unanimous support for international implementation. Nearly forty resolutions are passed each year. Most of them move on for further consideration by G77, a United Nations coalition of developing countries, while others are tabled for smaller groups of states to consider.

ECOFIN has played a role in passing impactful resolutions related to debt sustainability, international taxation, and other crucial issues. As a steward of economic and financial concerns in the United Nations, ECOFIN is a principal body in helping countries develop and the world achieve sustainable development. It has played a crucial role in the UN’s past and will in its future, too.

The growing sovereign debt crisis is putting significant economic and developmental pressure on developing countries due to increased borrowing, high interest rates, inflation, and slow global economic growth. High levels of debt are forcing governments to spend more on debt repayment, leaving fewer resources for healthcare, education, infrastructure, and climate-related needs. The involvement of different types of creditors, including private and bilateral lenders, has also made debt restructuring more difficult. Existing global debt systems have struggled to address these challenges due to slow restructuring processes, limited cooperation among creditors, and a lack of transparency. Therefore, ECOFIN must explore practical reforms to create a more effective, transparent, and sustainable system for managing sovereign debt.
agenda: Addressing the Rising Sovereign Debt Crisis in Developing Countries and Reforming Global Debt Architecture

mandate:
The International Court of Justice is an exacting and doctrinally foundational committee which positions delegates at the center of the most volatile debates in modern international law. Anchored in treaty interpretation and judicial rigor, this committee forces delegates to grapple with state sovereignty, asymmetric warfare, and evolving definitions of aggression. It grants advocates and judges the ultimate authority to interpret the UN Charter and reshape the limits of national defense. Delegates will become elite legal minds capable of balancing state survival, military necessity, and a rules-based international order in the face of modern security threats that have long outsmarted classical legal definitions and challenged the post-WWII framework from within.

This committee favors rigorous jurisprudence over diplomatic compromise and stresses international customary law over political alignments. Delegates craft arguments and opinions which are textually grounded, legally actionable, and precedent-focused, drawing inspiration from historical legal legacies including the Caroline criteria and the Nicaragua precedent. From reframing the threshold of an armed attack to protecting sovereign borders against proxy conflicts, the International Court of Justice invites delegates to determine the future of global conflict and accountability by the law and for the world.

After the Iranian Revolution in 1979, US policy toward Iran shifted from strategic alignment with the Shah to containment and conflict management. Israel’s long running concerns regarding Iran’s nuclear weapons programmes and regional influence helped drive its escalatory means of pressuring the Iranian state, often in tandem with the US, through various means of diplomacy, sanctions policy, intelligence, covert action and, at times, the direct use of force.

The conflict’s legal relevance for ICJ mainly arises because many key disputes were framed around the international legality of: the use of force, state responsibility for wrongful acts, economic coercion through sanctions, and compliance with, or denounced breaches of, treaty obligations, especially through the US–Iran treaty litigation at the ICJ.
agenda: USA–ISRAEL (APPLICANT) v. ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF IRAN (RESPONDENT) Preventive War vs Self-Defence: Interpretation of Article 51 of the UN Charter

mandate:
The Romanov court was the imperial court of Russia during the House of Romanov, the dynasty that ruled Russia for 303 years from 1613 until the February Revolution of 1917. The committee will represent the tsar, grand dukes and duchesses, boyars, court officials, Orthodox Church leaders, military commanders, and foreign ambassadors as they try to navigate the complexity of absolute monarchy from the dynasty’s founding after the Time of Trouble under Michael I to its collapse during the February Revolution of 1917 under Nicholas II, the last Russian monarch usurped by the revolution).

The Romanov court served as the center of government and power for the Russian Empire, with several key functions. These included the tsar, who made all major political, military, and diplomatic decisions. Court officials managed the vast civil service, including taxation, performing rituals and ceremonies that reinforced the Tsar’s divine right to rule, and acting directly as Russia’s military command during wars. The delegates in the committee will represent historical figures and discuss major political decisions such as reforming versus maintaining absolute autocracy, Russia’s WWI military defeat, any response to strikes, food shortages and revolutionary movements and will respond to any crisis updates to determine the fate of the Romanov Dynasty.

The years 1916 and 1917 were a tipping point for the Russian Empire and the Romanov dynasty. Nicholas II's autocratic rule was out of touch with the needs of the people. The limited measures taken after the first Russian revolution of 1905 were ineffective. The Russian involvement in WWI created an even more disastrous situation characterized by military defeats, an economy in shambles, and a deficit of food and other basic needs. The Tsar's decision to head the army in 1915 caused the people to blame the defeats on the monarchy.

Further decreasing confidence in the government was Tsar Nicholas II’s refusal to cooperate with the State Duma and his dismissal of reform proposals. His isolation and the Crown’s refusal to implement reforms decayed what support the court had from the elites and the public and strengthened radical opposition. The combination of economic crises, food shortages, and political stagnation in 1917 placed the imperial state on the brink of revolution and collapse and jeopardized the stability of the Romanov dynasty.
agenda: Preserving the Russian Empire Amidst Internal and External Crisis

mandate:
As science continues to redefine the limits of medicine, humanity stands at the threshold of a new era. Breakthroughs in longevity research and anti-ageing therapeutics promise the possibility of longer, healthier lives, but they also bring difficult questions that cannot be answered by science alone. If these innovations become accessible only to those with the means to afford them, the richest 5%, the world may face a future in which the quantity and quality of life itself are measured by wealth rather than equality. As hope and uncertainty go hand in hand, this issue extends far beyond healthcare; it becomes a question of global justice.

The World Health Organisation Committee for RBSMUN XXI will convene to examine this rapidly evolving global issue. As the international body entrusted with promoting health for all, the WHO finds itself at the centre of a debate that blends scientific innovation with ethics, law, and public policy. Delegates will explore whether the organisation possesses the mandate to guide or regulate the emerging anti-ageing therapeutics industry while at the same time considering how global cooperation can ensure that medical progress benefits humanity as a whole.

The stakes are profound: medical innovation, healthcare accessibility, economic disparity, and international responsibility converge in a debate that could shape the future of global health. Delegates will be challenged to balance scientific advancement with equitable access, encourage innovation while at the same time safeguarding human rights, and determine the role of the World Health Organisation in addressing one of the defining challenges of the twenty-first century. The decisions made in this committee may influence not only the future of healthcare governance but also whether the promise of longer, healthier lives becomes a shared achievement or remains a privilege enjoyed by only a select few.

The longevity industry has moved from speculative science to serious capital; biotech, AI, and precision medicine are converging to make "slowing ageing" a viable commercial product, not just a research goal. Investment is pouring in from pharma giants, venture capital, and tech billionaires betting on extended, healthier human lifespans. Yet beneath the promise lies a governance vacuum: no global body has clearly claimed the authority to regulate who gets access to these breakthroughs. This committee asks whether the WHO can, or should, step into that vacuum before the world splits into two demographics: those who age, and those who can afford not to. At stake is nothing less than the future shape of human mortality itself, and who gets to write its rules.
agenda: The Commercialization of Human Longevity — Whether WHO Has the Mandate to Regulate the Emerging Anti-Aging Therapeutics Industry Before It Creates a Two-Tiered Global Lifespan Divided Entirely by Wealth

mandate:
प्रतिनिधि सभा नेपालको संघीय संसदको तल्लो सदन हो। यसको मुख्य जिम्मेवारी राष्ट्रिय नीति निर्माण गर्ने, कानून तर्जु गर्ने र सरकारका कार्यहरूको निगरानी गर्नु हो। यस समितिमा सहभागीहरूले सांसद र राजनीतिक नेताको रूपमा भूमिका निर्वाह गर्नेछन्। उनीहरूले नेपालको राजनीतिक, आर्थिक र कूटनीतिक क्षेत्रका जटिल चुनौतीहरूमाथि गहन छलफल गर्नेछन्। यस समितिले नेपाली राजनीतिको वास्तविक स्वरूपलाई प्रतिविम्बित गर्नेछ, जहाँ गठबन्धन निर्माण, वार्ता, सहमति र रणनीतिक निर्णयहरूले राष्ट्रको भविष्य निर्धारण गर्दछन्।

यो समितिले सहभागीहरूलाई राष्ट्रिय तथा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय मुद्दाहरूको गहिरो विश्लेषण गर्न, नीति निर्माण गर्न र सरकारी गतिविधिहरूको समीक्षा गर्ने चुनौती प्रदान गर्नेछ। राजनीतिक गठबन्धन, कूटनीतिक वार्ता, कानूनी सुधार र संकट व्यवस्थापनका माध्यमबाट सहभागीहरूले शासन व्यवस्थाको व्यावहारिक अनुभव प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। यहाँ सफल हुनका लागि प्रभावकारी वक्तृत्वकला मात्र पर्याप्त हुने छैन; कूटनीति, नेतृत्व क्षमता, परिस्थिति अनुकूलनशीलता र राष्ट्रिय हितका लागि सहमति निर्माण गर्ने क्षमताले पनि महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका खेल्नेछन्।

यस एजेन्डा अन्तर्गत नेपालमा नयाँ सरकारको गठन तथा सञ्चालनका प्राथमिकताहरू, नयाँ राष्ट्रिय बजेट निर्माणका आधार र प्राथमिक क्षेत्रहरू, हालैको बाढीबाट भएको क्षति तथा त्यसको व्यवस्थापनबारे छलफल गरिनेछ। साथै, आगामी विकास परियोजनाहरूको प्राथमिकता निर्धारण, दिगो विकास तथा वातावरणीय जोखिम न्यूनीकरणका उपायहरू र दीर्घकालीन रूपमा विपद् व्यवस्थापन गर्न विदेशी राष्ट्र तथा अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय साझेदारहरूसँग गर्न सकिने सहकार्यबारे छलफल गरिनेछ।
agenda: नयाँ सरकारको गठन, नयाँ बजेट निर्माण, हालैको बाढी व्यवस्थापन, आगामी विकास परियोजना तथा दीर्घकालीन वातावरणीय संरक्षणका लागि अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय सहकार्यबारे छलफल।

fullname: The Grand Convocation of the Mythical Realms
mandate:
For millennia, the realms— the gods above, the mortals below, and the mythical beings between them—have existed in a delicate balance. The gods have the power to shape destinies, command nature, and enforce the order of the universe. That balance, however, has been shattered. Through his heist of fire from Mount Olympus, Prometheus was able to give humans the power of fire. This action did more than challenge divine command; it sparked the greatest debate the realms have ever witnessed: Does knowledge and power solely belong to the divine, or does every race have the right to pursue greatness?

The Grand Convocation of the Mythical Realms is a historic gathering unlike any before, bringing together the rulers of Olympus, legendary heroes, mortal leaders, and ancient creatures beyond mortal understanding. Called upon after the outcome of Prometheus’ rebellion, this council must confront the consequences of a world in which humans are no longer helpless. As fire spreads through the mortal realm, civilizations have begun to rise and prosper, and the age of divine supremacy is encountering its greatest challenge.

Should the gods tighten their control to preserve natural order, or should they accept that the lit fires cannot be extinguished? Should Prometheus be held as a criminal, or a hero who allowed for humanity to flourish? Due to such questions, this committee is not merely a discussion of power; it is a battle of ideals. Delegates must navigate between the ideals of authority or freedom, and immortality or ambition. The fate of Prometheus is only the beginning; the true question before the Grand Convocation remains whether the future belongs to those who have ruled for eternity, or for those who have begun to rise.

In an age long before the first pages of mortal history were written, when the gods still remained sovereign over the world, the realms— the gods above, the mortals below, and the mythical beings between them—have existed in a delicate balance. This balance, however, has been shattered due to Prometheus’ Theft of Fire. Through his initiative, humans have been shown that rebelling against the divine is possible, no matter what may be the consequences. Through his actions, Prometheus has sparked the greatest debate that the realms have ever witnessed: Does knowledge and power solely belong to the divine, or does every race have the right to seek greatness?
agenda: The Future of Divine Hegemony in an Age of Mortal Advancement: A look at Divine Authority following Prometheus’ Theft of Fire

mandate:
The United Nations Security Council is the leading organ of the international community, and it is uniquely charged under the UN Charter with the heavy responsibility of maintaining global peace and security. It has the exclusive power to implement economic sanctions and deploy military forces under its Chapter VII mandate. The success of this body hinges on whether its five permanent and ten elected member states can resolve their state-centric interests to enact collective security measures.

Repeated exchanges of attacks between the United States and Iran have once again demonstrated how a regional conflict can swiftly jeopardize global order, key energy routes, and the international trade system. As risks escalate around the Strait of Hormuz, nations across the world fear a spike in energy prices and disruptions of supply chains. The volume of oil that typically passes through this strategic waterway roughly equates to one-fifth of global petroleum consumption, making its security a matter of international concern rather than a matter of regional interest alone. The geopolitical clash between two nations carries profound consequences for states around the globe.

The United Nations Security Council shall serve as the primary forum for negotiation and pacification for the cause of international peace and security. Through constructive, tactful, and pragmatic policy frameworks, member states work collectively to safeguard critical trade chokepoints and ensure the uninterrupted flow of international commerce. This council will focus on both immediate measures to contain the crisis and long-term solutions that will reinforce economic resilience and adherence to international law.

Political tensions rarely remain purely political when they endanger transnational mobility. Repeated exchange of attacks between the United States and Iran is unfolding in a region whose strategic geopolitical importance extends far beyond its borders, making the stability of its trade networks a matter of international concern.

As risks escalate around the Strait of Hormuz, through which around one-fifth of global petroleum liquids consumption typically passes, nations across the world fear spikes in energy prices and supply chain disruptions.The vessel traffic now raises questions about how long alternative routes and supply sources can shoulder the pressure. The consequences may therefore extend beyond immediate price rises: prolonged disruption could reshape shipping patterns, energy trade and the economic decisions of countries far removed from the conflict itself.
agenda: Addressing the ongoing crisis in the Middle East between the United States and Iran, and its effect on international trade

mandate:
“The wheel of history is inexorably turning: he who cannot keep pace with it shall be crushed. ” ~Khmer Rouge

The year is 1989. Two decades of war have hollowed Cambodia out — first as collateral to a conflict it never chose, then as a laboratory for an ideology that mistook erasure for renewal. Nearly two million lives were extinguished under the Khmer Rouge's pursuit of Year Zero, and though Vietnam's 1979 invasion ended the killing, it did not end the war. It merely changed its shape.

Now, as the Cold War loosens its grip and Vietnamese troops withdraw, the international community assembles in Paris for one last attempt at resolution. The PICC brings together the four Cambodian factions, the P5, ASEAN, and the wider world — all mandated to forge a comprehensive political settlement. But peace is never simple when the perpetrators of genocide still sit at the table, when great powers pursue their own interests beneath the language of diplomacy, and when a nation's fate rests on whether its enemies can agree.

Will delegates rise to the moment, or will Cambodia be condemned to further discord?

fullname: United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women
mandate:
As technology advances at an unprecedented pace, the digital world has become a space of both opportunity and danger. While artificial intelligence has opened new possibilities for communication, creativity, and progress, it has also introduced emerging threats that challenge the safety and dignity of women and girls. The misuse of AI through deepfakes, online harassment, cyberstalking, and other forms of digital abuse has created a growing global concern that requires immediate and collective action.

The United Nations Entity for Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women (UN Women) will convene to address the emerging issue of technology-facilitated violence against women and girls, a modern challenge that threatens gender equality, human rights, and the ability of individuals to participate safely in the digital world.

Delegates will be tasked with developing effective and inclusive solutions to prevent digital abuse, strengthen international cooperation, support survivors, and ensure the responsible use of emerging technologies. The future of online safety and the protection of women and girls in the digital age will depend on the decisions and commitments made by this committee.

The proliferation of technology facilitated violence, including deepfakes, cyberstalking, AI enabled abuse and online harassment, poses an escalating threat to the safety, dignity, and fundamental rights of women and girls globally. Undermining gender equality and equitable digital participation, this crisis demands urgent multilateral action. UN Women will convene to formulate inclusive, survivor-centered frameworks that prevent digital violence, strengthen international cooperation, and ensure the ethical governance of emerging technologies.
agenda: Addressing Technology-Facilitated Violence Against Women and Girls in the Age of AI and Deepfakes

mandate:
The United Nations Human Rights Council is an intergovernmental body within the United Nations system made up of 47 states responsible for the promotion and protection of all human rights around the globe. It has the ability to discuss all human rights issues and situations that require its attention throughout the year.

As the world races toward a clean future, a dark cost is buried beneath the very ground that promises to save us. The minerals powering our clean energy future are extracted at devastating human cost.

The United Nations Human Rights Council will convene to examine the hidden toll of the global green energy transition. It is a crisis in which the pursuit of climate progress collides with the rights and dignity of vulnerable communities.

The stakes are high. The cobalt mines of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, for example, are tainted by child labor and hazardous conditions, and the drought-stricken lands of South America's Lithium Triangle, where indigenous communities watch their water vanish into foreign supply chains, Both, as well as other, similar conditions, reveal an uncomfortable truth about the cost of clean energy. Delegates will be tasked with confronting the practices of powerful corporations and consuming nations as well as crafting solutions that neither halt climate progress nor sacrifice the rights of those who bear its burden. The path forward must reconcile environmental urgency with human dignity. The choices made in this committee will shape whether the green revolution becomes a story of justice or exploitation.

As the world progresses towards the utilization of ‘clean energy’ in an attempt to combat the ever looming threat of global warming and climate change, the workers in the supply chains for the production of such energy are plagued by severe human rights violations. The ever growing demand for critical minerals, in this case lithium, cobalt, copper and more, has caused worldwide labor exploitation, including child labour, hazardous working conditions and more. Further issues like water depletion, toxic pollution and more impact local ecosystems, harm indigenous communities and contribute to the very crisis the clean energy movement was created to mitigate. The UNHRC will convene in order to establish a rights based framework, working to enforce transparency in the nature of supply chains, and ensure that advancements in clean energy do not come at the cost of human rights and dignity.
agenda: Stopping human rights abuses in green energy supply chains

The United States Congress is the legislative branch of the federal government of the U.S. The House of Representatives and the Senate form a bicameral legislature, with the Senate serving as the upper house. Congress meets in the United States Capitol in Washington, D.C. Although vacancies in the Senate may be filled by the appointment of the governor, senators are usually elected by direct election. There are 100 senators (two from each of 50 states) and 435 representatives in the House of Representatives. Their number is determined by the population of each state. The vice president of the United States has a vote in the Senate only when the number of senators is evenly split. No votes will be cast by six members of Congress.

Every other January, a new Congress convenes for a two-year tenure. Elections are conducted every even-numbered year on Election Day. Senators serve a six-year term, with one-third being elected every two years. Representatives serve two years.

Gun violence remains a major and deeply contested issue in the United States. While there is broad discussion around reducing firearm-related harm, disagreements often arise over the role of the federal government, the extent of firearm regulation, and how much responsibility should fall on states and local communities. This agenda will explore both federal firearm regulations and community-based approaches to preventing violence, while considering issues such as constitutional rights, enforcement, access to firearms, and the different circumstances faced by communities across the country. Delegates should aim to examine the issue from multiple perspectives and consider solutions that address both immediate risks and the underlying causes of violence.
agenda: Addressing Gun Violence in the United States Through Federal Firearm Regulation and Community Safety Measures.

mandate:
The Social, Humanitarian, and Cultural Committee (SOCHUM) is the Third Committee of the United Nations General Assembly. Its mandate encompasses human rights, social development, humanitarian affairs, and the protection of vulnerable populations. SOCHUM tackles the problems associated with the empowerment of women and children, the integration of refugees, and the eradication of systemic discrimination targeting race and ethnicity. In addition, it focuses on youth empowerment, family welfare, ageing populations, disability rights, crime prevention, criminal justice, and international drug control.

At RBSMUN2026, SOCHUM will address the urgent humanitarian and security crises posed by illegal migration networks (“dunki [donkey] routes”) across Asia, Europe, and North America. It will discuss the perilous conditions faced by migrants in transit and craft cogent and collaborative solutions that include dismantling trafficking networks, reducing reliance on smugglers, improving humanitarian aid, and elevating policies that uphold human rights and dignity.

Dunki routes are illegal migration routes where people travel through multiple countries to reach their final destination without following legal immigration procedures. These journeys often involve agents or smugglers, leaving migrants vulnerable to exploitation, trafficking, and unsafe conditions. At the same time, these routes create security concerns by making border monitoring more difficult and enabling various criminal networks. This makes dunki migration both a humanitarian and security issue. The issue is especially important across Asia, Europe, and North America, where migration routes cross several borders. Countries need to cooperate to identify and disrupt these networks while also protecting the vulnerable migrants.
agenda: Addressing the security and humanitarian issues posed by illegal migration networks (Dunki Routes) across Asia, Europe and North America

The International Press Corporation is the backbone of MUN documentation: it unites journalists who document committee proceedings and craft opinion pieces based on their insights. The IPC also conducts interviews, produces feature stories, and blogs highlighting key decisions made in the United Nations. Through its work, the IPC amplifies delegate voices and creates a culture of complex debate and journalistic excellence.

The main goal of the IPC is perfection when it comes to paperwork, but it also fosters thoughtful debate amongst journalists from different newspapers, who will aim to attain consensus regarding the agenda. The objective is not to enforce rigid rules but to instead spark thoughtful discussion about where ethical and legal parameters should lie, ensuring accountability while also respecting legitimate security concerns. Journalists must navigate dilemmas like protecting sources without justifying misinformation, demanding transparency without compromising safety, and reporting the truth without abusing press freedom.

The contentious dichotomy between Freedom of Speech and the Right to Reputation constitutes a profound hurdle to modern society, where uninhibited expression must coexist with the protection of individual dignity and social standing. Legal, ethical, and societal tension is explored when the exercise of free expression potentially besmirches another person’s reputation. Reporters will explore the extent to which governments, institutions, and individuals should be permitted to regulate defamatory, malicious, or harmful speech without inadvertently facilitating censorship or suppressing legitimate dissent. Particular attention will be given to the responsibilities of accompanying freedom of expression, including the proliferation of misinformation, digital communication, journalistic accountability, and the evolving influence of social media. Reporters must seek to illuminate and highlight mechanisms capable of reconciling public discourse with meaningful safeguards against unjustified reputational injury.
agenda: Freedom of Speech VS Right to Reputation
